heading: Raaka: What world record has Allu Arjun-Atlee’s film created a year before release?
paragraphs: The upcoming sci-fi film, Raaka, directed by Atlee and featuring actors Allu Arjun and Deepika Padukone, has entered the Guinness World Records for the “Most People Motion-Captured in Real-Time.” Produced by Sun Pictures’ Kalanithi Maran, the record was set after 37 performers were captured simultaneously in a single session, marking a notable technological milestone for Indian cinema.

Achieved during production in February 2026, the record was officially certified on September 15. Swapnil Dangrikar, Senior Adjudicator at Guinness World Records, presented the certificate to lead actor Allu Arjun and director Atlee at a ceremony attended by the film’s core cast and crew.

Actor Allu Arjun, while speaking about the honour, said, “We are extremely proud of this remarkable achievement, which pushes the boundaries of cinema and sets a new benchmark on a global scale. It is a proud moment for the entire team, and we are grateful to Guinness World Records for officially recognising this feat and honouring our efforts. This achievement would not have been possible without the vision and direction of my director, Mr Atlee, and the incredible work of the entire team. I would also like to thank Sun Pictures for their constant support and for backing a project of this scale and ambition. It is a truly special moment for all of us.”

Director Atlee added, “Growing up, we always heard about Guinness World Records with so much wonder, never imagining that one day we would be blessed to achieve one ourselves. To receive this recognition for bringing 37 motion-capture assets together in a single shoot feels truly surreal and deeply humbling. For me, it is a reminder that when we dream big and work together with complete belief, sometimes the impossible becomes possible. With God’s grace, I’m deeply grateful to my entire team who believed in this dream and made this moment ours.”

During the shoot, 37 performers — ranging from a four-year-old child to a 70-year-old — were motion-captured in real time within a single capture volume. The primary technical hurdle lay in tracking each individual actor's movement data simultaneously without signal loss or spatial distortion.

To achieve the record, the visual effects team engineered a custom motion-capture pipeline tailored to the production's technical demands. The setup deployed 92 optical motion-capture cameras alongside Unreal Engine for real-time visualisation, synchronised witness feeds, and facial tracking technology to manage live data stream calibration.
Earlier, the makers had shared a cryptic 'global triumph' slogan alongside a '37' hint, offering another glimpse into the scale of the upcoming film.
The technical achievement was a collaborative effort between Sun Pictures, lead actor Allu Arjun, Apple Art Studio, and the production's visual effects crew.
Beyond the record, Raaka highlights the rising technical scale of domestic cinema, demonstrating how Indian productions are expanding their in-house virtual production capabilities.
The technological feat underscores how Indian sci-fi productions are expanding the scope and execution of Indian visual effects on an international scale.
Raaka also features actors Mrunal Thakur, Janhvi Kapoor and Rashmika Mandanna in key roles.
